Flow: Tithes and offerings (often taught as 10%). Stated purpose: They are said to support mission and staff.. How it controls: Giving becomes a test of worthiness and loyalty, and members who cannot afford it give out of guilt.. Who benefits: The money goes to the institution, clergy salaries and building debt..

Flow: Building campaigns and capital pledges. Stated purpose: They are said to fund facilities for ministry.. How it controls: Multi-year pledges bind members financially to an institution they may want to leave.. Who benefits: The institution and its construction and consulting vendors benefit..

Flow: Unpaid volunteer labor. Stated purpose: It is framed as service and the use of spiritual gifts.. How it controls: It works as extraction: the leadership is paid and the workforce is not, and the hours crowd out life outside the church.. Who benefits: The institution and its salaried staff benefit..

Flow: Media, books, conferences, worship licensing. Stated purpose: They are offered as teaching and resources.. How it controls: They are sold to a captive audience, and the pastor's personal intellectual property is monetized through the congregation.. Who benefits: Individual leaders, publishers and record labels benefit..
